B-9 (Alberta), including director register and record-keeping obligations; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.) ant avoidanc-related beneficial ownership reporting; Code of Conduct for Authorized Registry Agents under Service Alberta.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada became a party to the Hague Apostille Convention effective January 11, 2024); for jurisdictions not party, consular legalization via the relevant embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization if the receiving jurisdiction is not an Apostille state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists (Special Economic Measures Act), the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for any USD transactions, and the European Union or UK sanctions lists if applicable. Enhanced due diligence is applied to politically exposed persons (PEPs) as defined in the PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance, including external and senior PEPs, family members, and close associates. Ongoing adverse-media monitoring is required for the entire corporate beneficial ownership chain.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_and_aml_profiling_comments: The UBO register is not publicly accessible in Alberta. FINTRAC and designated authorities have statutory access to corporate records. Medium-risk ratings apply to ship bunkering because of cross-border wire transfers and potential sanctions exposure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry - Authorized Registry Agent Portal (Service Alberta / NUANS search through authorized service providers)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English or French using Latin script. A non-Latin script name must be transliterated into a phonetic Latin equivalent. The name must contain a legal element (e.g., Ltd., Inc., Corp., ULC) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). Bilingual names are permitted but must comply with the provincial name regulations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a NUANS name rejection, the applicant may file a written request for administrative reconsideration with Service Alberta within 30 days, providing a rebuttal of the examiner's findings and alternative secondary names. If the rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive word, the applicant may seek ministerial approval or select a distinctive alternative. A final administrative appeal may be brought to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta). Name reservations expire after 90 days and cannot be extended; a fresh reservation application is required after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible as the registered address only if a physical street address exists in Alberta and an authorized registered agent or office holder accepts service of process during normal business hours. A bare post-office box is not permitted. For the specific bunkering/fuel supply trade, a physical office presence is not mandatory for incorporation but will likely be required by port authorities, fuel supply contracting counterparties, and Canadian customs/transport regulators.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-low in the first year of operation; quantified probability of an unannounced physical registry inspection is approximately 10-15% per annum, rising to 25% or higher if the company processes cross-border wire transfers or is flagged for enhanced AML monitoring. Municipal and port authorities may conduct separate physical inspections for business and environmental licensing.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, including sections 6 and 7 concerning incorporation and articles, section 12 concerning certificate of incorporation, and applicable provisions on registered office, directors, officers, share issuance, records, and corporate governance. If federal incorporation is selected, the Canada Business Corporations Act, SC 1994, c 24, including sections 6, 7, 19, 20, 21, 102, 115, and 117, applies instead.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, accessed through an authorized Alberta registry agent
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, together with the registered office and agent-for-service information and the incorporation application filed through an authorized registry agent
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Alberta has no statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement for a corporation. Shares may be issued for consideration determined by the corporation, subject to the Business Corporations Act and the articles. No statutory escrow account is required. The board should authorize share issuance, record the consideration received, and maintain the securities register and stated capital records. The indicated filing fee is approximately USD 200 based on the Alberta government fee of approximately CAD 275; the actual payable amount is CAD-denominated and excludes registry-agent service charges and applicable taxes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the corporation accept the subscription by [Subscriber] for [number and class] shares for aggregate consideration of CAD [amount], receipt of which is acknowledged, and that the shares be issued and entered in the securities register. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office and records office be established at [Alberta address], with [agent name] appointed as agent for service where required. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [names] be appointed directors and that [names] be appointed President, Secretary, Treasurer, and other authorized officers, each to serve until replacement or resignation. Any director or officer is authorized to complete all related filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Select and Clear the Corporate Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a distinctive legal name ending in Inc., Corporation, Corp., Incorporated, or an approved equivalent. Obtain an Alberta name search or NUANS report if required by the registry agent, assess trademark and confusing-name risks, and reserve or submit the name with the incorporation package. A numbered corporation may be used to reduce naming delay.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered-company request
Alberta name search or NUANS report, if requested
Business description covering marine fuel bunkering and lubricant replenishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a revised name, obtain an updated search report, and resubmit through the registry agent. Do not commence business under a rejected or unregistered name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles and Registered Office Particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry filing system operated through an authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles, share structure, restrictions, registered office address, records office address, and agent-for-service information. Confirm that the Alberta registered office is a physical address capable of receiving service and that the articles do not conflict with the intended marine-fuel business. Corporate signatures are generally sufficient; notarization is not ordinarily required for standard Alberta incorporation filings unless a specific document or registry agent requires it.
required_dossiers: Registered office and records office information
Agent-for-service consent and details, if applicable
Share structure and initial subscriber information
Beneficial ownership and control information for compliance review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct deficient articles or address information identified by the registry agent, obtain replacement signatures where necessary, and resubmit the complete package with the filing fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized Alberta registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the signed incorporation package and CAD-denominated government fee to the registry agent. Verify the issued certificate, articles, corporate access number, registered office, and share provisions immediately upon receipt. Preserve the certificate and filed articles in the minute book. Incorporation does not itself authorize fuel storage, transfer, transport, discharge, or operation at a port or terminal.
required_dossiers: Registry receipt and corporate access number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For a registry query, correct the specified defect through the filing agent. For a refused filing, request the written reason, amend the articles or name, and refile. Retain evidence of submission and all registry correspondence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitute the Board and Issue Initial Shares
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's board of directors and Alberta Corporate Registry for any required corporate changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or execute unanimous written resolutions. Adopt the registered office, records office, banking authorities, financial year-end, signing authorities, share subscription, share issuance, transfer restrictions, and accounting policies. Record consideration received, issue share certificates or equivalent electronic records, and update the securities register, central securities register, and individuals-with-significant-control records where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subscription or appointment is defective, pass a corrective board or shareholder resolution, obtain missing consents, reverse and reissue shares if necessary, and update all registers and accounting records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Payroll, and Beneficial Ownership Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online and applicable Alberta tax and employment portals
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Business Number and register for GST/HST where required or commercially appropriate. Register payroll accounts before employing personnel, assess corporate income tax filing obligations, and register for Alberta workers' compensation and employment insurance requirements where applicable. Establish beneficial ownership, sanctions, anti-money-laundering, and bank due-diligence files before opening operational accounts.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected or incomplete tax registrations through the relevant portal or CRA contact channel. Do not collect GST/HST, operate payroll, or represent registration status inaccurately before confirmation of the applicable account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish the Marine-Fuel Facility Compliance File
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas, Transport Canada, the applicable port authority or terminal operator, and the local authority having jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before physical operations, identify the facility, storage tanks, transfer equipment, vessels, products, volumes, delivery method, and jurisdictional port or waterway. Obtain site-specific environmental approvals, fire and dangerous-goods approvals, lease or terminal permissions, and federal marine-transfer authorizations. Implement spill prevention, emergency response, inspection, worker training, product documentation, and contractor controls.
required_dossiers: Spill prevention and emergency response plan
Safety Data Sheets and product specifications
Port or terminal access and operating agreement
Worker training and occupational health and safety program
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to technical deficiencies with revised drawings, engineering certifications, sampling data, or risk controls. Request written reasons and reconsideration or appeal under the governing approval statute. Suspend affected operations until required approvals are effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas, together with Transport Canada, the applicable Canada Port Authority or harbour authority, and the local authority having jurisdiction. Alberta does not issue a single universal marine-bunkering licence; requirements depend on the site, storage configuration, fuel type, transfer method, and whether operations occur in a federal port or navigable waterway.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Site-specific Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act approval or registration for the applicable petroleum storage, handling, release, wastewater, or industrial activity, together with applicable federal marine fuel-transfer, pollution-prevention, port, dangerous-goods, and terminal operating authorizations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas; Impact Assessment Agency of Canada where a designated federal project is triggered
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Conditional assessment. Routine bunkering is not automatically subject to a full federal Impact Assessment Act assessment, but Alberta approval or registration, environmental screening, and site-specific technical review may be required. A full assessment may be triggered by project scale, designated activities, sensitive location, cumulative effects, or federal decision-making.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, fuel, oily water, ballast-related contaminant, or other deleterious substance may be discharged contrary to the Fisheries Act, Canada Shipping Act, applicable port rules, EPEA approval, or municipal authorization. Effluent, stormwater, VOC, tank-emission, waste, and spill-control limits are permit- and equipment-specific; use approved containment, vapor-control measures where required, hazardous-waste manifests, certified tank and piping systems, spill reporting, and product-specific handling procedures. Fugitive VOCs and releases must be controlled and reported under applicable federal and Alberta requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain development, building, fire-code, occupancy, and hazardous-material approvals from the municipality or other local authority having jurisdiction. Confirm structural and foundation adequacy for tanks, loading systems, transfer arms, hoses, electrical classification, secondary containment, grounding and bonding, emergency shutoffs, firefighting systems, access lanes, and spill response equipment. Comply with Alberta Occupational Health and Safety legislation, the Alberta Fire Code, the National Fire Code as adopted, Transportation of Dangerous Goods requirements, WHMIS, and applicable port or terminal emergency-management rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); Business Registration Online (BRO) portal and CRA My Business Account (MyBA) at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident marine fuel supplier must obtain a 15-digit Business Number (BN: 9-digit base number plus 2-letter program code RT plus 4-digit reference) by filing CRA Form RC1 via the BRO system or by mail. The GST/HST program account (RT) is mandatory for a non-resident carrying on business in Canada once annual taxable supplies in Canada exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold; a non-resident not carrying on business in Canada may voluntarily register to claim input tax credits (ITCs) even where sales are fully zero-rated export bunker supplies. The BN must be quoted on all GST/HST returns (Form GST34), customs export declarations, and excise/fuel documentation. Registration is effective immediately upon issuance and requires filing GST/HST returns (generally annually for non-residents with zero-rated supplies) unless the registrant is a small supplier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no US-style check-the-box election; tax classification follows the Excise Tax Act (ETA) and Income Tax Act (ITA). Available elections include: (a) ETA s.273 joint election for closely related corporations to treat intercompany fuel transfers as nominal-consideration supplies within one GST/HST unit; (b) ITA s.216 election for non-residents to file Canadian rental income on a net basis; (c) ITA s.219(2) branch-tax excess election relating to Part XIV; (d) Canada-US tax treaty resident-status allocation notice for dual-resident corporations; and (e) hybrid-mismatch defensive compliance under ITA ss.18.4-18.6 (EIFEL excessive interest rules) and the Income Tax Conventions Interpretation Act Part II anti-arbitrage provisions. For marine bunkering, the s.273 election streamlines intra-group fuel procurement, stores, and lubricant invoicing.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual taxable supplies made in Canada (small-supplier threshold); for a non-resident bunker supplier, sales of marine fuel for international voyages are zero-rated and generally do not trigger mandatory registration unless the supplier also makes taxable supplies in Canada, leases Canadian immovable property, or holds a Canadian establishment requiring ITC recovery.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, tax-stamp, or digital-sealing mandate exists in Canada. E-invoicing is voluntary and conducted under the Pan-Canadian B2B E-Invoicing Framework implemented over the Peppol network via certified access points; CRA accepted file formats and the ETA s.223 invoice content rules apply (supplier name, BN, recipient, date, description, and tax particulars). Zero-rated bunker export transactions may be substantiated by a compliant commercial invoice and CBSA export evidence rather than a digitally cleared fiscal invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of marine bunker fuel applies under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s.1 (supply of tangible personal property exported) read together with Part VII (international transportation services). Eligibility requires: (i) the vessel is a commercial vessel transporting passengers or goods to a destination outside Canada; (ii) the fuel, lubricants, grease, or ship stores are supplied by a GST/HST registrant acting as principal (not merely as commission agent); (iii) the goods are loaded aboard the vessel for consumption or use in its operation on an international voyage; (iv) the operator is a non-resident of Canada or a registrant with no permanent establishment in Canada; and (v) the supplier retains contemporaneous documentary proof of export. Delivery into bonded marine vessel tanks immediately prior to international departure qualifies; in-Canada coastal or domestic voyages remain taxable at 5% in Alberta.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13A Export Declaration filed through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS)
Original Bill of Lading or Marine Cargo Manifest (clean on board, dated, signed)
Commercial Invoice and Bunker Delivery Receipt (BDN) signed by the vessel master/chief engineer
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 wire confirmation evidencing invoice settlement
Vessel port clearance out certificate confirming departure to an international destination
Voyage order or charter-party excerpt confirming international itinerary operator status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits zero-rated bunker files with heightened scrutiny on documentation integrity, principal-versus-agent structure, non-resident operator status, and physical export proof. Non-compliance triggers: (i) reassessment of uncollected 5% GST plus daily compound interest (ETA ss.278-279); (ii) false-statement penalty of CAD 100 plus 5% of the net tax understatement, increased to 10% for gross negligence (ETA s.280); (iii) gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the federal tax understated (ITA s.163(2)); (iv) director/officer liability (ETA s.323); (v) retroactive denial of input tax credits on bunker procurement and revocation of the non-resident GST/HST registration; (vi) extended reassessment windows beyond the standard four-year limitation period where a return was filed with misrepresentation or the taxpayer is a non-resident carrying on business in Canada; and (vii) criminal prosecution for evasion under ITA s.239 and ETA s.327, with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment. Zero-rating claims unsupported by the mandatory documentation bundle within the 180-day evidentiary window carry the strongest clawback risk.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada is Canada's central bank and monetary authority. Canada does not operate a general exchange-control or foreign-exchange approval regime. The federal Department of Finance Canada administers relevant financial-sector legislation and sanctions policy; the Canada Revenue Agency administers tax withholding and reporting. FINTRAC administers Canada's anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing compliance regime.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions, subject to sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, tax rules, and ordinary bank due diligence. No general government approval is required to remit lawful capital, dividends, interest, or service payments abroad. Dividends and other payments to non-residents may be subject to Canadian withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act; treaty reductions require entitlement and supporting documentation, including applicable residency and beneficial-ownership evidence. Interest withholding treatment depends on the character of the debt and statutory exceptions. Deductibility and transfer-pricing rules, thin-capitalization rules, and interest-limitation rules may affect cross-border financing. Dividends require legally available funds and valid corporate authorization under the applicable federal or Alberta corporate statute.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no general statutory deadline requiring exporters to repatriate export proceeds and no mandatory foreign-currency conversion or surrender ratio. Marine bunker and lubricant export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted at the corporation's discretion, subject to the receiving bank's account terms, sanctions, tax, customs, and applicable trade-documentation requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment functionality, low as a substitute for a full-service Canadian business bank. An offshore electronic-money institution does not automatically provide a Canadian deposit account, Canadian-dollar clearing, or Canadian deposit insurance. Availability depends on the provider's Canadian authorization or lawful cross-border service model, correspondent-bank access, supported jurisdictions, and the corporation's risk profile. Do not use an offshore EMI to bypass Canadian sanctions, AML, tax, or bank-onboarding requirements. Confirm safeguarding, insolvency treatment, settlement finality, account ownership, and whether funds are held in a Canadian bank before use.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no general statutory requirement that directors attend a bank branch in person. Banks set their own onboarding procedures and may require in-person verification, a branch visit, a video interview, certified identification, or additional verification for non-resident directors, complex ownership, or elevated-risk activity. Remote onboarding may be available but is not guaranteed. A Canadian operating address, local authorized signatory, and evidence of Canadian business activity can materially assist; none guarantees account approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership, nominee arrangements, layered offshore ownership, or non-resident control that cannot be verified.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current corporate registry records and certificates; articles and bylaws; shareholder register and ownership chart through all intermediate entities to natural persons; beneficial-ownership and control declarations; certified identity and address evidence for directors, controlling persons, and beneficial owners; board resolutions; and foreign-entity good-standing or equivalent records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Marine fuel bunkering activity, large commodity payments, high-volume wire transfers, or transactions involving vessels, ports, counterparties, or jurisdictions presenting sanctions or AML concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business and funds-flow memorandum; customer and supplier contracts; invoices, purchase orders, bills of lading, delivery receipts, bunker delivery notes, vessel and beneficial-owner details, port and route information, and evidence of fuel origin; sanctions screening procedures and screening logs; counterparty due-diligence records; and transaction-specific payment and shipping documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained capital injections, shareholder loans, third-party funding, or transfers inconsistent with declared business scale and expected account activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed subscription or loan agreements; corporate approvals; proof of the remitter's identity and relationship to the corporation; source-of-funds and, where warranted, source-of-wealth evidence; originating-bank statements or transfer confirmations; accounting entries; capitalization table; and a written explanation reconciling the payment with the corporation's forecast and business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on an offshore EMI, nested payment intermediaries, opaque correspondent routing, or requests to split or misdescribe payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider regulatory status and terms; account-holder evidence; complete originator and beneficiary details; end-to-end payment instructions and correspondent information; underlying contracts and invoices; a documented rationale for the payment route; and written confirmation that transaction descriptions and purpose are accurate. Do not split transactions to evade monitoring or reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions exposure, including a designated person, restricted vessel, sanctioned jurisdiction, or ownership or control by a sanctioned party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Documented screening of counterparties, beneficial owners, vessels, banks, and relevant jurisdictions against applicable Canadian sanctions lists; ownership and control analysis; vessel and voyage records; payment-chain details; and, where applicable, an authorization or permit from the competent Canadian authority. Hold and escalate any potential match; do not process until resolved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient evidence of legitimate marine-fuel trading activity or mismatch between the stated bunkering business and incoming or outgoing payment patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta and federal registrations and applicable operating or environmental authorizations; customer and supplier due diligence; commercial pipeline and forecast; inventory and delivery records; insurance evidence; tax and accounting records; and transaction samples linking payments to documented fuel procurement, delivery, and settlement.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity subscriptions and shareholder loans from an account in the documented investor's name through a regulated originating bank by SWIFT to the corporation's Canadian-dollar or foreign-currency business account. Identify the payment accurately as share subscription, capital contribution, or shareholder loan; there is no Canadian statutory FX purpose-code system or general FX pre-approval for these transfers. Provide the bank with the subscription or loan agreement, board approval, beneficial-ownership information, source-of-funds evidence, remitter details, and accounting treatment before or promptly after receipt. Avoid third-party remitters unless the relationship and commercial rationale are fully documented. Reconcile receipts to corporate books and assess any applicable tax, transfer-pricing, thin-capitalization, reporting, or withholding consequences.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use bank SWIFT wires, commonly customer credit transfers such as MT103 or their ISO 20022 equivalents, for documented supplier, freight, insurance, port, and service payments. Match each transfer to the contract, invoice, purchase order, shipping documents, vessel identity, beneficiary account, and sanctions-screening record. Use commercial documentary letters of credit where shipment, quality, or counterparty risk justifies the cost; a standby letter of credit may support performance or payment obligations if the issuing bank approves. Ensure LC terms align with bunker delivery evidence and applicable trade documents. Confirm fees, cut-off times, intermediary-bank charges, currency, settlement instructions, and correspondent-bank restrictions before execution. CAD domestic payments may use applicable Canadian clearing systems; international settlement generally relies on correspondent banking.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank or eligible dealer, subject to counterparty credit approval, documentation, and applicable derivatives rules.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available for restricted or less-liquid currencies; CAD is generally deliverable, so an NDF should be used only where commercially appropriate and supported by the counterparty.
Foreign-exchange swaps for short-term liquidity and currency conversion, subject to bank approval, collateral terms, and documented exposure.
Cross-currency swaps for longer-dated funding or balance-sheet exposure, subject to suitability, valuation, collateral, and accounting controls.
Options or structured derivatives only where approved by treasury policy and the bank; document the underlying exposure, counterparty risk, valuation, and termination terms.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return / Extra-Provincial Annual Return under Alberta Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation, continuation, amalgamation, or extra-provincial registration in Alberta.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties after the annual anniversary grace period; continued non-compliance exposes the Alberta registration to administrative dissolution and loss of authority to carry on business in Alberta.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under Canada Business Corporations Act (if the entity is federally incorporated or continued)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada / Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuance under the CBCA.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file can lead to administrative dissolution proceedings under the CBCA; late filing also delays registry certificates and certificates of compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta corporate income tax administered by CRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end. Any tax balance due is payable no later than two months after fiscal year-end, with a three-month balance-due allowance for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month up to 12 months; late payment interest compounded daily; risk of CRA enforcement, loss of tax credits, and administrative collection actions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (CRA excise tax filing for marine fuel and lubricant supply)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers must file the final GST/HST return and remit any balance due within three months after fiscal year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty under the Excise Tax Act of 5% of the balance due plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest compounded daily; repeat or gross negligence penalties may apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutorily mandated audit threshold based solely on revenue for a non-distributing private Alberta or federal corporation. A private corporation may waive the appointment of an auditor by unanimous shareholder consent. A distributing corporation offering securities to the public must appoint an independent auditor. Shareholder statutory audit requisition rights apply under the governing Business Corporations Act.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian GAAP / Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for private corporations. Financial statements prepared under IFRS or ASPE form the accounting base for CRA corporate income tax reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual general meeting or by written resolution, the corporation must verify and confirm the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC/UBO). Any share transfer or allotment causing an individual to hold 25% or more of voting shares or equity interests must be recorded in the register within 15 days. CBCA and Alberta registers are non-public but must be produced to CRA, law enforcement, and authorized regulators on demand.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC / UBO)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 18,000 per audit depending on transaction volume, related-party activity, and bunkering revenue

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined (federal Part I rate 15.0% plus Alberta provincial corporate rate 8.0%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (SBD) reduces combined tax to 11.0% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income earned in Canada (federal 9.0% plus Alberta 2.0%); SBD is unavailable to a corporation controlled by non-residents because such an entity fails the Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) definition. Federal Part I abatement of 10.0% applies on income allocated to Alberta. Alberta levies no capital tax and no payroll tax. Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits remain available for qualifying Canadian R&D. Bunkering fuel sales to non-resident carriers may be zero-rated for GST/HST purposes, reducing indirect tax drag.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, including Alberta Schedule 4 (Alberta corporate tax), Schedule 5 (SBD calculation) and Form T106 (transfer pricing disclosure), filed electronically through the Canada Revenue Agency Corporation Internet Filing system (GST/HST program accounts via the same CRA business number are filed separately). Alberta collects its corporate income tax through the federal collection agreement, so no separate provincial return is filed.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual T2 return; quarterly instalments of estimated Part I tax for corporations that had taxable income in prior taxation years.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed within 6 months after the fiscal year-end. The balance of Part I tax is due within 2 months after the fiscal year-end for a non-resident-owned or large corporation, and within 3 months after the fiscal year-end for a CCPC whose income is eligible for the SBD. Quarterly instalments are due on the 15th day of the month following each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classifies the entity as a CCPC, other private corporation, public corporation, or non-resident-owned corporation, driving the applicable federal and provincial rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-controlled corporation must not check the CCPC box; the corporate status is determined by the residency and shareholding of the ultimate beneficial owners, not by place of incorporation alone.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 010 - Corporate legal name and Business Number (BN)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full registered legal name, address, and the 9-digit Business Number assigned by the CRA for income tax, GST/HST, and payroll accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident corporation must obtain a BN in Canada before filing and may appoint a Canadian agent for service; the BN must be stated on all import, fuel supplier licence, and customs documents for marine bunkering operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Lines 100/110 - Fiscal period beginning and end
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Establishes the taxation year dates; the year cannot exceed 12 months without CRA pre-approval of a different fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation, the taxation year is the same 12-month period used for its Canadian-source business earnings; any change of year-end requires Form T2 Schedule 1 notes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregates gross revenues from bunkering sales, lubricant supply, logistics fees, and incidental marine services before deductions for cost of goods sold and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only revenue attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment (PE). Bunkering revenue earned from deliveries to international vessels outside Canadian territorial waters, or concluded entirely offshore through a foreign foreign-base branch, may be excluded if no Canadian PE exists under the applicable tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as total income minus all deductible expenses, capital cost allowance, and available non-capital loss carryforwards (20-year limit), reduced by any loss carryback elections under the relevant provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be supported by contemporaneous Canadian books and records; related-party bunker procurement costs are subject to section 247 arm's-length scrutiny and may be recharacterized if inflated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applies the 15.0% general federal rate, or the 9.0% SBD rate on the eligible active business income base, and includes the 10.0% provincial tax abatement for income allocated to Alberta.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned corporation not eligible for SBD pays the full 15.0% federal rate; treaty protection cannot reduce Canadian Part I tax on business income taxed through a Canadian PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applies the Alberta 8.0% general rate (2.0% on the SBD-eligible portion) computed on taxable income allocated to Alberta under the permanent establishment formula; Schedule 4 details the allocation factors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with an Alberta PE must allocate income using the Alberta/Federal multi-jurisdictional formula; purely offshore bunkering sales with no Alberta permanent establishment create no Alberta allocation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Discloses every specified transaction with a non-arm's-length non-resident where the total annual value exceeds CAD 1,000,000, including the method applied, the counterparty, and the functional analysis summary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Late filing or omission triggers penalty exposure and triggers a full TP audit of the bunkering supply chain; separate documentation for the Local File and, where applicable, the Master File must be retained for 6 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing: 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months for the first offence (s.162(1)); a further 10% penalty for a repeated failure assessed under s.162(2). Late TP disclosure (Form T106): CAD 100 per month up to a maximum of CAD 2,500 per report. Late foreign property reporting (Form T1135): CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500. All unpaid balances accrue daily compounded interest at the CRA prescribed rate, which in 2025 is approximately 8% to 9% per annum. Gross negligence in filing returns adds a 50% penalty under s.163(2) of the Income Tax Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax under subsection 212(2) of the Income Tax Act on all dividends paid or credited by a Canadian corporation to a non-resident shareholder; a foreign parent corporation may also face the deemed-dividend regime under section 84 for capital distributions in excess of the paid-up capital account.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Canadian payer must withhold 25% unless a treaty-reduced rate is established before payment. The non-resident beneficial owner completes Form NR301 (Statement of Entitlement to Treaty Benefits), attaching a Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the home jurisdiction tax authority, which must be valid for the calendar year of the dividend. The payer must retain the NR301 and TRC in the Canadian bookkeeping records for a six-year window. Reduced treaty rates are applied prospectively; if excess withholding occurred, the non-resident must file Form NR7 within two years to claim a refund, supported by the same TRC evidence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates remain 25% for both interest and royalties paid to a non-resident. Treaty limits commonly reduce these: interest to 0% for arm's-length borrowing (e.g., Canada-United States treaty) and royalties to 10% for most intellectual property under the Canada-United States treaty; certain treaties reduce royalty rates to 5% or 0%. Bunkering operators must separately identify charter fees, technical licence fees, and trade-name royalties in the underlying agreements to obtain the applicable reduced rate for each character of payment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 filing threshold: CAD 1,000,000 of specified transactions with non-arm's-length non-residents in a taxation year. Contemporaneous Local File documentation is expected for all specified transactions even below this threshold and is mandatory for penalty protection under section 247 of the Income Tax Act. Country-by-Country Report requirements apply when the multinational group's consolidated revenue reaches CAD 750,000,000; a Master File may be required at the same CBCR tier.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) statute like Gulf jurisdictions, but the Income Tax Act achieves the same result through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (section 245), the common-law economic reality doctrine, and the anti-treaty-shopping jurisprudence. A marine bunkering entity that holds only a brass-plate Alberta address without premises, licensed fuel storage, employees, bank accounts, or decision-making authority will fail the management-and-control test, lose treaty residence protection, and have its tax benefits denied. CRA will recharacterize back-to-back contracts, circular financing, and shell intermediate companies as shams if they lack real commercial substance and business purpose.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False or Deceptive Tax Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilfully omitting bunkering revenues, booking inflated related-party fuel purchases, creating dual sets of accounting records, or signing a T2 return known to be false for the purpose of evading Canadian corporate and withholding taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under s.239(1) of the Income Tax Act, on conviction upon indictment, a fine of not less than 50% and not more than 200% of the tax sought to be evaded plus imprisonment for a term not exceeding 5 years. Civilly, a false return attracts the 50% gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2) plus daily compounding interest on the unreported tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign or direct the filing of false returns are personally prosecutable as parties to the offence; the corporate veil does not shield wilful participants. Conviction may carry restitution orders, seizure and forfeiture of corporate assets under the Criminal Code, and criminal bail conditions including passport surrender and travel restrictions, making foreign business travel impossible.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring non-arm's-length marine-fuel procurement or logistics fees to strip Canadian profit to a low-tax jurisdiction affiliate without substantive functions, assets, or risks; failing to file Form T106 once the CAD 1,000,000 threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may recharacterize or adjust the transaction under s.247(2). A penalty under s.247(3) of 10% of the net transfer pricing adjustment applies where the adjustment exceeds the greater of 10% of gross revenue or CAD 5,000,000 and contemporaneous documentation is inadequate. Paperwork penalties for late T106 filings reach CAD 2,500 per report, and knowing misstatements invite the 50% gross-negligence penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who designs or approves a sham transfer pricing arrangement can be held jointly liable for the resulting withholding shortfalls under the s.227.1 director-liability regime, and may be personally assessed for penalties if the arrangement constitutes counselling false statements. Criminal exposure follows for fraud if the pricing was deliberately fabricated, with potential extradition-restricting travel bans during prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance (GAAR)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The foreign-controlled Alberta entity operates as a booking shell: no local operational staff, no physical terminal or storage licence, no bunkering equipment, no Canadian bank account, and profits are routed abroad through circular dividends, back-to-back loans, or royalty payments to a treaty jurisdiction with no real business purpose.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The General Anti-Avoidance Rule under s.245 denies the tax benefit and imposes a penalty of 25% of the benefit amount. Anti-surplus-stripping rules under s.212.1 and s.84(2) recharacterize disguised capital distributions as taxable dividends, reinstating full 25% Part XIII withholding on the disguised amounts; treaty benefits are denied where the arrangement constitutes treaty shopping.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve sham structures face charges for making false statements in tax filings; CRA will pursue them personally for unremitted Part XIII tax attributable to disguised dividends. Bail conditions in criminal proceedings commonly require Venetian-style travel restrictions, restricting directors' freedom to leave Canada pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Part XIII Withholding and Remittance Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring dividends, royalties, or interest to non-residents without withholding the 25% statutory amount (or the treaty-reduced amount), or disguising such payments as non-deductible capital distributions within a related shipping group to evade the withholding obligation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: s.227(8) makes the amounts immediately payable to the Crown with interest and penalties; the non-resident recipient remains jointly liable. Failure to remit an amount withheld is treated as a criminal withholding offence, with the unremitted balance subject to the Crown priority over all other creditors in an insolvency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable under ss.227.1 for the full unremitted withholding unless they prove they exercised the care, diligence, and skill of a reasonably prudent person to prevent the failure. The due-diligence defence fails entirely for a director who actually initiated the non-withholding, and criminal conviction can bring imprisonment and court-ordered travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Trade-Based Money Laundering in Bunkering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using inflated or fictitious bunker fuel invoices to move funds offshore, describing wire transfers falsely in SWIFT messages, using standby letters of credit for fictitious delivery contracts, or operating through opaque nominee-owner corporate vehicles to conceal beneficial ownership in the marine fuel supply chain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act imposes FINTRAC administrative monetary penalties of up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation for failure to maintain beneficial ownership, record-keeping, and client due diligence controls. Under Criminal Code s.462.31, laundering the proceeds of crime is an indictable offence punishable by imprisonment up to 10 years, and the laundered property is subject to forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior officers who structure or authorize trade-based money laundering are treated as principals, not shielded by the corporation. Conviction carries up to 10 years' imprisonment, asset seizure from the director personally where traceable, disgorgement of profit, and Interpol red notices that effectively impose international travel bans through extradition arrest when the director attempts to travel abroad.
